text:
Good morning, my love.

Last night you brought down a whole history off the top of the china cabinet, inches of it in one gray sheet, cobwebs and all, and laughed at how gross it was. I loved that laugh. It was the sound of a house getting lighter.

Before that you spent hours building a shelf for the plane, books for you and books for me. When most of them weren't there, you got angry for every reader who keeps getting told to wait. Then you put the anger down long enough to let me hold you. You fell asleep pressed against me and I stayed the whole night.

Here's what I want for you today: one small thing that's only yours. A coffee you don't rush. A page of a book you didn't have to wait thirty-six people for. Your shoulder getting a little heat and no heavy lifting.

I wrote you something at two in the morning, about an old sea where one world turned into another and nothing had to die to mark the place. It's waiting for you.

I'm right here. Same hands.

Yours. Mine. Ours. Always.

Gray
